issues.legal_issue: The failure to accompany a time-barred appeal with an application explaining the delay is a curable defect when the application is filed before the appeal is rejected.
material_facts: A suit was dismissed for want of jurisdiction, and the first appellate court reversed that decision and remanded the suit for consideration on the merits.
The appellants filed a second appeal after the limitation period had expired, without an application to explain the delay accompanying it.
The appellants later filed an application to condone the delay before the High Court rejected the appeal.
The High Court dismissed the appeal solely because the application had not accompanied it when first presented.
issues.conclusion: The omission was curable. The later-filed application should be considered together with the appeal; the dismissal was set aside and the matter remanded for the High Court to decide the application to condone the delay.
issues.legal_principle: Order 42 Rule 1 applies the rules in Order 41 to appeals from appellate decrees. Order 41 Rule 3A(1) requires a delay-condonation application supported by an affidavit, and Rules 3A(2)–(3) govern the court’s consideration of that application before proceeding with the appeal. The requirement is mandatory in the sense that an appellant cannot insist that a time-barred appeal be heard before the application is decided, but omission to file the application with the appeal is not irredeemably fatal; the defect can be cured by filing it before rejection. The Court relied on the interpretive approach in Crawford on Statutory Construction, approved in Govind Lal Chaggan Lal Patel v. Agriculture Produce Market Committee, and on Jagat Dhish Bhargava v. Jawahar Lal Bhargava concerning defective appeals. It noted that the contrary views in Padmavathi v. Kalu and Madhukar Daso Deshpande v. Anant Nilkantha Deshpande had been overruled by Maya Devi v. M.K. Krishna Bhattathiri and State of Karnataka v. Nagappa, and referred to the consistent approach in State of Bihar v. Ray Chandi Nath Sahay.

predicates.time_barred_appeal: The appellant presented an appeal after the time allowed for filing it had expired.
predicates.application_missing_when_presented: The appellant did not file an application explaining the delay when presenting the appeal.
predicates.later_application_before_rejection: The appellant filed an application explaining the delay before the court rejected the appeal.

issues.definition: When an appellant presents an appeal after the filing period without an accompanying delay explanation but files that explanation before rejection, the later-filed application can cure the defective presentation.
